text:
alice: Hey team — since ~03:00 UTC we've been seeing intermittent TLS handshakes failing from apac-ingress -> eu-backend. Error in logs: 'x509: certificate signed by unknown authority' and occasional 'OCSP stapling: response invalid'.

ben: Ack. Any recent cert rotations or IAM changes for the keystore role?

alice: Not from app side. I checked deploys; nothing for the service in the last 48h. Saw a flurry of RBAC changes in infra on Tuesday though.

carol: I pulled the proxy logs. Sample stack:
```
2026-03-19T02:58:12Z proxy eu-backend tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate
x509: certificate signed by unknown authority (chain: /etc/ssl/certs/chain.pem)
```
Also noticed a KMS decrypt failure for the private key on one pod:
```
ERROR KMS Decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: kms:Decrypt
Principal: service-account:ingress-proxy@redwood-inference
Resource: arn:aws:kms:eu:.../alias/keystore
```

dave: That screams RBAC regression — last week we scoped the keystore role to require the new 'keystore-access' attribute. I pushed a policy patch but thought we tested it for all namespaces.

cert-bot: cert-rotator job failed for eu-proxy at 2026-03-19T03:01:00Z — reason: unable to decrypt private key using KMS alias/keystore (AccessDenied).

ben: If cert-rotator couldn't write a new key, some pods ended up with stale chain.pem pointing to an intermediate that was rotated out. That would cause unknown authority.

alice: Ok — action plan? Should we roll back the RBAC change and re-run the rotator, or attempt to re-grant Decrypt to the service-account only in eu region?

carol: Prefer minimal blast radius: grant kms:Decrypt to the specific SA for alias/keystore in eu for 1 hour, re-run rotation, validate chain, then tighten back. We should also check audit logs for when the role binding changed.

dave: I can do the temporary grant. Who will run the rotation and verify end-to-end? I'll also add an IAM permission exception in the ticket.

alice: @dave please do the grant. @carol can you re-run rotator and post verification steps? I'll page oncall if this looks like broader outage.

carol: Re-running rotator docs snippet I'm using:
```
kubectl -n infra exec job/cert-rotator -- /bin/sh -c "./rotate.sh --service eu-proxy --kms-alias alias/keystore --output /tmp/new.pem"
# then deploy secret sync
kubectl -n eu rollout restart deploy/eu-backend
```
I'll also validate with `openssl s_client -connect eu-backend.service.consul:443 -servername eu-backend` and confirm CA chain.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3492 — apac->eu TLS handshake failures. Severity: P2. Assigned: dave.

dave: Grant applied to service-account for 1h. Policy id: iam-exception-2026-03-19-01. Please re-run rotator now.

carol: Running... rotator completed ✅. Updated chain.pem contains intermediate ID: int-2026-02-15-v3. Ran openssl check: certificate chain validated, OCSP stapling responded GOOD.

alice: I'm seeing reduced error rate in logs — handshake failures dropped to near zero. Still a few old pods with cached secrets, doing rolling restarts.

ben: We should follow up with a postmortem: root cause appears to be RBAC tightening without adding rotator SA to new role binding. Also need tighter CI gate that simulates rotator KMS decrypts after permission changes.

carol: Agreed. Also propose: add an alert for KMS Decrypt failures from cert-rotator (>=3 in 5m) and a healthcheck for cert-rotator job success in region.

dave: I'll open a tracking ticket for IAM change process: link to ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-1876. Will include checklist: 1) update rolebindings for rotator, 2) run smoke rotation in staging, 3) verify audit logs, 4) notify sec/oncall.

alice: For immediate hardening: set TLS profile to enforce min TLS1.3 on east-west traffic where supported, drop legacy ciphers, but ensure all proxies can handle TLS1.3. This reduces attack surface and mismatched behavior.

ben: Also recommend: signoff step whenever a cert-rotator IAM change is planned. Add to runbook: "If rotator SA loses kms:Decrypt -> failover to cached certs + alert + temp allow via IAM exception."

carol: I'll write the runbook update and add an automated playbook for temporary grant with TTL and audit annotation.

dave: Final status: GRANT removed at 2026-03-19T04:00Z, cluster healthy. I'll attach logs to INFRA-1876 and loop in compliance for audit trail.

alice: Thanks everyone. Postmortem + runbook update expected EOD. :thumbsup:
